reasoning:
To find the characteristic polynomial of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10 & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14 \end{pmatrix}$, we compute $p(\lambda) = \det(A - \lambda I)$.

$$A - \lambda I = \begin{pmatrix} -4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:
$$p(\lambda) = (-4-\lambda) \det \begin{pmatrix} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} - (-13) \det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} + 10 \det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Evaluating the 2x2 determinants:
1. $\det \begin{pmatrix} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = (10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - (-20) = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120$
2. $\det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = (-9)(-14-\lambda) - 48 = 9\lambda + 78$
3. $\det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{pmatrix} = 45 - 12(10-\lambda) = 12\lambda - 75$

Substituting these back into the determinant expansion:
$$p(\lambda) = (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(9\lambda + 78) + 10(12\lambda - 75)$$
$$p(\lambda) = (-\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480) + (117\lambda + 1014) + (120\lambda - 750)$$
$$p(\lambda) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744$$

We can verify this using the trace and determinant of $A$:
- Trace of $A$ (sum of diagonal elements) $= -4 + 10 - 14 = -8$. The coefficient of $\lambda^2$ in $p(\lambda)$ is $-(-8) = 8$, which matches.
- Determinant of $A$ is calculated as $(-4)(-110) - (-13)(78) + 10(-75) = 440 + 1014 - 750 = 704$.
Wait, evaluating $\det(A)$: 
$-4(10 \times -14 - 4 \times -5) - (-13)(-9 \times -14 - 4 \times 12) + 10(-9 \times -5 - 10 \times 12)$
$= -4(-140 + 20) + 13(126 - 48) + 10(45 - 120)$
$= -4(-120) + 13(78) + 10(-75)$
$= 480 + 1014 - 750 = 744$.
The constant term of $p(\lambda)$ is $\det(A) = 744$, which matches.
